2.title: 青少年、漫畫與暢銷玩具
2.instruction: Chau 一家正在博物館內，談論剛看過的展品。請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。

女孩漫畫

3.title: 年輕發明家
3.instruction: Chau 一家正在博物館參觀名為「年輕發明家」的展覽，由導賞員帶領。請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。
blocks: 發明一：鞋子電池充電器
發明者姓名：Juan Domingo。
構思來源
發明者每天步行五公里上學（例子）。他發覺這是 {{32}}。一般人平均會走 {{33}}。
發明的運作原理
步驟一：踏在 {{34}} 上。步驟二：腳步產生 {{35}}。步驟三：這轉化為電力。步驟四：電力儲存在電池內，電池裝在 {{36}}。
用途例子
{{37}} 九十分鐘＝足供 {{38}} 使用十五分鐘的電力。鞋子的另一用途：{{39}}。
第 40 題：誰認為這項發明有用？（可選一項或以上。）A Angela；B Chau 先生；C Chau 太太。
發明二：氣味鬧鐘
發明者姓名：Jean-Paul Moncoeur。
構思來源
其他詳情
最有效的氣味是 {{43}}。裝置會朝着熟睡的人 {{44}}。大部分人醒來時 {{45}}，而且 {{46}}。
第 47 題：誰喜歡這項發明？（可選一項或以上。）A Angela；B Chau 先生；C Chau 太太。

4.title: James Dean 與《阿飛正傳》
4.instruction: Chau 一家正在聽 David Stott 的講座，主題是受年輕人歡迎的影星。請聆聽講座，回答以下問題。不必以完整句子作答。第一項已作為例子。
blocks: 圖片：James Dean。
即使未看過 James Dean 的電影，人們仍可能透過哪三種方式認識他？
提出兩個他至今仍如此有名的原因。

電影《阿飛正傳》（Rebel Without a Cause）有何特別？{{53}}
在《阿飛正傳》之前，年輕人在電影中扮演什麼類型的角色？{{54}}

1.speaker: Exam Narrator
1.text: Task 1. The Chau family is searching on the internet and talking about things to do. Listen to their discussion and write the information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example.
1.zh: 任務一。Chau 一家正在上網搜尋，討論可以做些什麼。請聆聽他們的討論，把資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。

1.speaker: Exam Narrator
1.text: You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
1.zh: 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。任務結束後，你將有一分鐘整理答案。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: So then, let's plan what to do today. Any ideas?
1.zh: 那麼，我們計劃一下今天做什麼吧。有什麼主意？

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Let's just go for a walk around the centre of London.
1.zh: 不如在倫敦市中心四處逛逛。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: But Dad, the centre of London is really big. And it's too much walking. Let's do something else.
1.zh: 但爸爸，倫敦市中心很大，要走太多路了。做點其他事吧。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Well, how about going to a museum? London has lots of excellent museums according to this website your Dad is looking at. Here are some exhibitions.
1.zh: 不如去博物館？爸爸正在看的網站說，倫敦有很多出色的博物館。這裡有一些展覽。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: But museums are boring. Can't we do something more fun?
1.zh: 但博物館很悶。我們不能做些更有趣的事嗎？

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Not all museums are boring. Have a look at this one. It's the Video Games Museum.
1.zh: 不是所有博物館都沉悶。看看這個，電子遊戲博物館。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Oh yes, that sounds interesting. What kind of video games do they have?
1.zh: 噢，聽起來有趣。它有什麼類型的電子遊戲？

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Let's have a look.
1.zh: 看看吧。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Oh, they have all kinds of video games, including a very early video game from 1958 called Tennis for Two.
1.zh: 它有各種電子遊戲，包括一款很早期、1958 年推出、叫 Tennis for Two 的遊戲。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Tennis for what?
1.zh: Tennis for 什麼？

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Tennis for Two.
1.zh: Tennis for Two，即《雙人網球》。

1.speaker: Chau family
1.text: Oh yes, and there's another one called Ping Pong from 1972. I remember that one. It's like table tennis. When is it from again?
1.zh: 還有另一款叫 Ping Pong，是 1972 年的。我記得它，像乒乓球。它是哪一年推出的？

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: That's so old! Are there any new games?
1.zh: 這麼古老！有新遊戲嗎？

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: How about this one?
1.zh: 這個怎麼樣？

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Teen Queen Four.
1.zh: Teen Queen Four，即《少女女王》第四集。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: That's from this year, 2016. And all my friends have Teen Queen Four.
1.zh: 那是今年，即 2016 年推出的。我的朋友都有 Teen Queen Four。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Is there a Teen Queen Five?
1.zh: 有 Teen Queen Five 嗎？

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: No Dad, don't be silly. That's for next year.
1.zh: 沒有啦，爸爸，別傻了。那是明年的。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Shall we go there then? Sounds good to me.
1.zh: 那我們去這裡吧？我覺得不錯。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Let's have a look at the opening times. Oh no, it's closed on Wednesdays so we can't go today.
1.zh: 看看開放時間。糟了，星期三休館，今天去不了。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Oh.
1.zh: 噢。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Well, it's not the end of the world. We can go another day. Any other ideas?
1.zh: 又不是世界末日，可以改天再去。有其他主意嗎？

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: What about this one? The Railway Museum.
1.zh: 這個呢？鐵路博物館。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: The Railway Museum?
1.zh: 鐵路博物館？

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Yes.
1.zh: 對。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: That sounds boring.
1.zh: 聽起來很悶。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Maybe not.
1.zh: 未必吧。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: It's in an old station and you get to ride on an old train.
1.zh: 它設於舊車站內，而且可以乘搭古老的火車。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Actually, that does sound boring. Boring.
1.zh: 其實那真的很悶。很悶。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: No, it's not boring. And it's quite cheap too. It's only 250 Hong Kong dollars per person.
1.zh: 不，不悶，而且相當便宜，每人只需港幣二百五十元。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: 250 dollars per person? That's expensive.
1.zh: 每人二百五十元？很貴。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Yes, too expensive.
1.zh: 對，太貴了。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Plus it's boring.
1.zh: 而且很悶。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Okay then.
1.zh: 那好吧。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: I guess you're right. Let's look for something else.
1.zh: 我想你們說得對，再找別的吧。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: How about this one?
1.zh: 這個怎麼樣？

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: The Museum of Youth Culture. Youth Culture? That sounds all right.
1.zh: 青年文化博物館。青年文化？聽起來還不錯。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: There's an exhibition about toy ponies. One of your favourite toys.
1.zh: 有一個關於玩具小馬的展覽，那是你最喜歡的玩具之一。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: You've still got your collection of toy ponies, haven't you? The My Pony Collection.
1.zh: 你還留着那套玩具小馬收藏吧？就是 My Pony Collection。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Yes, but I don't play with my ponies very much now. I'm a bit too old.
1.zh: 有，但我現在很少玩小馬了。我有點過了玩的年紀。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: But you still like them.
1.zh: 但你仍然喜歡它們。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Yeah, I suppose so.
1.zh: 嗯，應該是吧。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Do you want to go see the exhibition of toy ponies?
1.zh: 你想去看玩具小馬展覽嗎？

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Yes, okay. There's also an exhibition about boy bands. I don't like boy bands anymore.
1.zh: 好啊。這裡還有關於男子組合的展覽，但我已不再喜歡男子組合。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: I thought you did.
1.zh: 我以為你喜歡。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Nope.
1.zh: 不喜歡了。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: How about this?
1.zh: 這個呢？

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: There's an exhibition on children's fashion. That sounds boring.
1.zh: 有一個兒童時裝展覽，聽起來很悶。

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: No, but have a look at some of these pictures of the clothes. Don't they look interesting?
1.zh: 不，看看這些服裝圖片，不覺得很有趣嗎？

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Oh yeah. Those clothes look pretty cool. I'd like to see that exhibition.
1.zh: 噢，對，那些衣服很酷。我想看這個展覽。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Finally, we've got a museum. Let's have a look at where the museum is. Oh no, it's quite far away. Let's have a look.
1.zh: 終於找到一間博物館了。看看它在哪裡。噢，距離挺遠。讓我看看。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: Oh, but it's open late today.
1.zh: 不過今天開放到很晚。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: Okay, so we can go there later. How much is it?
1.zh: 那可以遲些去。門票多少錢？

1.speaker: Mrs Chau
1.text: Oh look, it's free for school children on Wednesdays. That means it's free for Angela today.
1.zh: 看，星期三學童免費，所以 Angela 今天不用付錢。

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: And one more thing.
1.zh: 還有一點。

1.speaker: Angela Chau
1.text: What?
1.zh: 什麼？

1.speaker: Mr Chau
1.text: It's interesting for all of us.
1.zh: 我們所有人都會覺得有趣。

1.speaker: Exam Narrator
1.text: That is the end of task one. You now have one minute to tidy up your answers.
1.zh: 任務一完結。你現在有一分鐘整理答案。

2.speaker: Exam Narrator
2.text: Task two. The Chau family are in the museum. They are talking about what they have just seen.
2.zh: 任務二。Chau 一家正在博物館內，談論剛才看過的展品。

2.speaker: Exam Narrator
2.text: Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. You now have 30 seconds to study the task. At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
2.zh: 請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。任務結束後，你將有一分鐘整理答案。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: So what did you two see?
2.zh: 你們兩個看了什麼？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: We saw an exhibition on Teenagers and Comics of the World.
2.zh: 我們看了「青少年與世界漫畫」展覽。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: Was it interesting?
2.zh: 有趣嗎？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Oh yeah, it was brilliant. There are loads of comics just for girls.
2.zh: 有啊，精彩極了。有很多專為女孩而設的漫畫。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: Really? I never knew that. I thought all the comics would be for boys.
2.zh: 真的？我從不知道，我以為漫畫都是給男孩看的。

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: That's what I thought too. But there are so many for girls. Particularly Japanese comics.
2.zh: 我原本也這樣想，但其實有很多給女孩看的，尤其是日本漫畫。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: Oh really? What are they like? Are they violent?
2.zh: 真的？內容怎樣？有暴力嗎？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Of course not, Mum. Duh, I said comics for girls. Not boys.
2.zh: 當然沒有啦，媽媽。我說是女孩漫畫，不是男孩漫畫。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: So what are they like then?
2.zh: 那內容是怎樣的？

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: Well, there are two main kinds of comics for girls. The first kind's fantasy. What kind of fantasy? Can you give me an example? Okay, I suppose the most popular kind is a superhero comic.
2.zh: 女孩漫畫主要有兩類，第一類是幻想題材。哪類幻想？能舉例嗎？我想最受歡迎的就是超級英雄漫畫。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: And what about the other kind?
2.zh: 另一類呢？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Well, the other main kind's real life. For example, school life.
2.zh: 另一大類是現實生活，例如校園生活。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: You seem to know a lot about comic books.
2.zh: 你似乎很熟悉漫畫。

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Oh yeah, I read them all the time.
2.zh: 是啊，我經常看。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: I didn't know that. But where do you buy them?
2.zh: 我不知道呢。你在哪裡買？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: There's a shop I go to in Electric Road.
2.zh: 我會去電氣道的一間店。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: Electric Road? Why do you go there? Why not the place near our home?
2.zh: 電氣道？為什麼到那裡？不去家附近那間嗎？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: There's a much better choice there.
2.zh: 那裡的選擇多得多。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: I'm not sure I like the idea of you buying comics.
2.zh: 我不太肯定是否喜歡你買漫畫。

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Oh, it's not what you think. These are comic books for teenagers. They're not violent at all. They're about problems teenagers have.
2.zh: 不是你想的那樣。這些是給青少年看的漫畫，完全沒有暴力，內容關於青少年面對的問題。

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: Problems teenagers have? Like what?
2.zh: 青少年的問題？例如什麼？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Arguing with parents. I mean, we're arguing now. That's a problem for me.
2.zh: 跟父母爭執。例如我們現在就在爭執，對我來說就是個問題。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Ha ha, very funny. Look you two, let's stop this. What did you see, Linda?
2.zh: 哈哈，真好笑。你們兩個別吵了。Linda，你看了什麼？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: I saw an exhibition on best-selling toys from the past.
2.zh: 我看了「昔日暢銷玩具」展覽。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Oh, that sounds interesting. What did they have?
2.zh: 聽起來有趣，有什麼展品？

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: Well, one of the things they had was a Cabbage Patch doll. It was really popular in the 1980s. That doesn't sound very exciting. Ah, but this doll is actually really ugly.
2.zh: 其中一樣是 Cabbage Patch Doll，它在二十世紀八十年代很流行。聽來不太精彩啊。不過這個娃娃其實很醜。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Really? Why would anyone want a doll like that?
2.zh: 真的？誰會想要這樣的娃娃？

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: But that's the whole point. People bought the doll because it was ugly. I really can't believe that. How many little girls would want one? Well, actually millions of little girls.
2.zh: 這就是重點，人們正因為它醜才買它。難以置信，有多少小女孩會想要？事實上有數以百萬計。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Why were they so popular?
2.zh: 它為什麼這麼受歡迎？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: Well, I think it's because there were many different designs.
2.zh: 我想是因為有許多不同款式。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Many different designs?
2.zh: 許多不同款式？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: Yes, and this made them very collectible.
2.zh: 對，因此很有收藏價值。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: So, ugly, but collectible dolls. Do you want one for your birthday, Angela?
2.zh: 所以是很醜、但值得收藏的娃娃。Angela，你想要它做生日禮物嗎？

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Actually, I'd quite like one. I can look after it for a few years, so it increases in price.
2.zh: 其實我挺想要。我可以好好保存幾年，讓它升值。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: That's my girl, always thinking ahead. What else did you see, Linda?
2.zh: 這才是我的女兒，總是想得長遠。Linda，你還看了什麼？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: Um, I saw one other thing that I think you would really like.
2.zh: 還有一樣，我想你會很喜歡。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Which is?
2.zh: 是什麼？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: A space hopper.
2.zh: 彈跳球。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: A what?
2.zh: 什麼？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: A space hopper. It's like a big rubber ball.
2.zh: 彈跳球，就像一個大橡膠球。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: A big rubber ball?
2.zh: 大橡膠球？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: Yes, and you sit on it and jump around.
2.zh: 對，你坐在上面四處跳。

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Wow, jumping around. That sounds kind of fun.
2.zh: 嘩，跳來跳去，聽起來挺好玩。

2.speaker: Chau family
2.text: But the best part was the extra things. You know the other things that kids used to do with space hoppers. Like what? Well, you can have a race.
2.zh: 最好玩的是其他玩法，就是以前小朋友會用彈跳球玩的其他遊戲。例如什麼？例如比賽競速。

2.speaker: Mr Chau
2.text: Actually, me and my brother both had one. And as well as having races, it was really good fun having a fight.
2.zh: 其實我和弟弟以前各有一個。除了比賽，拿來打鬧也很好玩。

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: You and your brother fighting. That doesn't surprise me.
2.zh: 你跟弟弟打鬧？一點也不意外。

2.speaker: Angela Chau
2.text: Actually, this toy is beginning to sound awesome. Can we go back and see it, Mum?
2.zh: 這玩具聽起來愈來愈棒。媽媽，我們可以回去看看嗎？

2.speaker: Mrs Chau
2.text: Sure, let's go.
2.zh: 當然，走吧。

2.speaker: Exam Narrator
2.text: That is the end of task two. You now have one minute to tidy up your answer.
2.zh: 任務二完結。你現在有一分鐘整理答案。

3.speaker: Exam Narrator
3.text: Task three. The Chau family are looking at an exhibition in the museum called Young Inventors. A guide is showing them around this exhibition. Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below. The first one has been provided as an example. You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
3.zh: 任務三。Chau 一家正在博物館參觀名為「年輕發明家」的展覽，由導賞員帶領。請聆聽錄音，把缺漏資料填入以下空格。第一項已作為例子。你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。

3.speaker: Exam Narrator
3.text: At the end of the task, you will have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers.
3.zh: 任務結束後，你將有一分半鐘整理答案。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Sakari Douglas and I'll be your guide for this section of the museum. Today, I'll be showing you the exhibition on Young Inventors and I hope you enjoy the tour.
3.zh: 大家好，我叫 Sakari Douglas，是博物館這個展區的導賞員。今天會帶大家參觀「年輕發明家」展覽，希望各位享受導賞。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: It sounds really interesting. Do you think it will inspire you to try some inventions of your own, Angela?
3.zh: 聽起來很有趣。Angela，你覺得這會啟發你嘗試自己的發明嗎？

3.speaker: Angela Chau
3.text: Not likely. I'm no good at science.
3.zh: 不大可能，我不擅長科學。

3.speaker: Mr Chau
3.text: But I don't think all the inventions are about science. Let's have a look at them.
3.zh: 但我想不是所有發明都與科學有關，先看看吧。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: So, our first exhibit is the Shoe Battery Charger. This was invented by Juan Domingo from the Philippines and he was only 14 when he invented it. The inventor walks five kilometers to school every day. I know this seems a lot, but in the countryside in the Philippines, many school children have to do the same. Anyway, the inventor thought that this is a lot of wasted energy.
3.zh: 第一件展品是鞋子電池充電器，由菲律賓的 Juan Domingo 發明，當時他只有十四歲。他每天步行五公里上學。我知道看來很遠，但在菲律賓鄉郊，很多學童都一樣。他想到，這其實浪費了很多能量。

3.speaker: Mr Chau
3.text: Wow. A five kilometer walk to school every day? That's pretty far. Would you like to walk that far to school, Angela?
3.zh: 嘩，每天走五公里上學？挺遠的。Angela，你願意走那麼遠上學嗎？

3.speaker: Angela Chau
3.text: Not likely. I'm not going to waste all that energy.
3.zh: 不可能，我才不會浪費那麼多能量。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Well, actually, according to the inventor, on average, people take 7,000 footsteps a day.
3.zh: 其實，根據發明者所說，人們平均每天走七千步。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: That seems a lot. So how does the shoe work?
3.zh: 似乎很多。那鞋子怎樣運作？

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Well, there are different stages to the process and let me show you. Here is the shoe and inside each shoe are two electrical discs. First, the person wearing the shoe steps on the electrical discs every time they take a footstep. Second, each footstep generates pressure on the disc. And third, this pressure is then converted to electricity.
3.zh: 過程分幾個階段，我示範一下。這是鞋子，每隻鞋內有兩塊電力圓片。第一，穿鞋者每走一步都會踩到圓片。第二，每步會對圓片產生壓力。第三，壓力轉化為電力。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: So how do you store the electricity?
3.zh: 那怎樣儲存電力？

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: You need a battery and you attach it to the outside of your shoes.
3.zh: 需要一顆電池，把它裝在鞋子外面。

3.speaker: Angela Chau／Museum Guide
3.text: I've got a question. Yes. How much electricity do the shoes generate?
3.zh: 我有問題。請說。鞋子能產生多少電力？

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: That's a good question, actually. At the moment, not so much. But this is the first model. The inventor gave an example of when he played basketball for an hour and a half. He managed to generate 15 minutes of battery power for a mobile phone.
3.zh: 好問題。現時不太多，但這只是第一個型號。發明者舉例說，他打了一個半小時籃球，產生的電池電量足夠手機使用十五分鐘。

3.speaker: Angela Chau
3.text: That's not very much.
3.zh: 不算很多。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: That's right. But there is one other application that the inventor has suggested. This electricity can be used to power a light and this doesn't need so much power. Any other questions?
3.zh: 對，不過發明者另提了一種用途：電力可以用來照明，而燈所需的電量較少。還有問題嗎？

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: What do you think, Angela?
3.zh: Angela，你覺得怎樣？

3.speaker: Angela Chau
3.text: Well, I wouldn't like to do all the walking, but it certainly is useful.
3.zh: 我不想走那麼多路，但它肯定有用。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: What do you think, Dad?
3.zh: 爸爸，你覺得呢？

3.speaker: Mr Chau
3.text: I think it's great.
3.zh: 我覺得很棒。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: I worry that it's not practical, and you won't be able to produce enough electricity. Surely, traditional batteries are better.
3.zh: 我擔心它不實用，產生不了足夠電力。傳統電池應該更好吧。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Okay, let's move on to our next invention. Just over here. Can everybody see?
3.zh: 我們看下一項發明，就在這裡。大家看得到嗎？

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: This invention is the smelly alarm clock. The inventor of this is Jean-Paul Moncoeur, and he's from Canada. This 17-year-old invented the device for his father, who is deaf, or hard of hearing, I should say. Jean-Paul invented this to help his father, who couldn't hear the sound of an alarm clock. As a result of this, very often his father was late for work and almost lost his job.
3.zh: 這是氣味鬧鐘，發明者是加拿大的 Jean-Paul Moncoeur。這位十七歲少年為父親發明了它；父親失聰，或更準確地說是聽力不佳，聽不到鬧鐘聲，因此經常上班遲到，幾乎失去工作。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Jean-Paul had the brilliant idea of using the sense of smell instead of sound to wake people up.
3.zh: Jean-Paul 想到一個妙計：用嗅覺代替聲音，喚醒睡覺的人。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: Sorry to interrupt, but what smell did Jean-Paul find was the most effective to wake people up?
3.zh: 抱歉打斷一下，Jean-Paul 發現哪種氣味最能喚醒人？

3.speaker: Chau family／Museum Guide
3.text: That's a good question, and the answer is peppermint. Peppermint? Yes, peppermint.
3.zh: 好問題，答案是薄荷。薄荷？對，薄荷。

3.speaker: Mr Chau
3.text: So, how does the device work then?
3.zh: 這裝置怎樣運作？

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Well, first you place some peppermint tablets inside the alarm clock, and then you set the alarm. When the alarm goes off, a fan blows air towards the sleeper.
3.zh: 首先把薄荷片放入鬧鐘，再設定鬧鐘時間。鬧鐘啟動時，風扇會向睡着的人吹氣。

3.speaker: Angela Chau
3.text: But does it really work?
3.zh: 但真的有效嗎？

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: Oh yes, and you know that most people hate getting up early in the morning. Well, the inventor reckons that most people wake up in a good mood.
3.zh: 有，而且你知道大部分人都討厭清早起床。發明者認為，大部分人醒來時心情愉快。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: Really, that sounds good to me.
3.zh: 真的？聽起來不錯。

3.speaker: Mr Chau
3.text: Mmm, sounds too good to be true to me.
3.zh: 嗯，對我來說聽起來好得令人難以置信。

3.speaker: Museum Guide (Sakari Douglas)
3.text: And one more thing, apparently you also wake up feeling refreshed.
3.zh: 還有一點，據說醒來後也會感到精神煥發。

3.speaker: Mr Chau
3.text: No, I'm not convinced.
3.zh: 不，我還未被說服。

3.speaker: Mrs Chau
3.text: I am? I think it sounds fantastic. What do you think, Angela?
3.zh: 我就信了。我覺得很棒。Angela，你怎麼看？

3.speaker: Angela Chau
3.text: I think I agree with Dad on this one.
3.zh: 這次我想我同意爸爸。

3.speaker: Exam Narrator
3.text: That is the end of task three. You now have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers.
3.zh: 任務三完結。你現在有一分半鐘整理答案。

4.speaker: Exam Narrator
4.text: Task four. The Chau family are attending a lecture given by David Stott about movie stars that are popular with young people.
4.zh: 任務四。Chau 一家正在聽 David Stott 的講座，主題是受年輕人歡迎的電影明星。

4.speaker: Exam Narrator
4.text: Listen to the lecture and answer the questions below. Please note, you do not need to answer in complete sentences.
4.zh: 請聆聽講座，回答下列問題。注意：不必用完整句子作答。

4.speaker: Exam Narrator
4.text: The first one has been provided as an example.

4.speaker: Exam Narrator
4.text: You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
4.zh: 你現在有三十秒閱讀題目。

4.speaker: Exam Narrator
4.text: At the end of the task, you will have two minutes to tidy up your answers.
4.zh: 任務結束後，你將有兩分鐘整理答案。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: Hello everyone. My name is David Stott and I'm here to talk to you about one American movie star from the 1950s who has perhaps had the biggest influence on young people all over the world. So, who is this movie star? Well, of course, it's James Dean. Even if you don't know his name or have never seen him in a movie, you still might recognize him. How? Well, you might see his image in a work of art such as a painting or a screen print.
4.zh: 大家好，我叫 David Stott。今天要談一位二十世紀五十年代的美國影星，他可能是對全球年輕人影響最大的影星。他是誰？當然是 James Dean。即使不知道他的名字、從未看過他的電影，你仍可能認得他。怎樣認得？你可能在油畫或絲網版畫等藝術作品中見過他的形象。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: He has featured in some of the most famous art of the last century. Apart from art, you might see a photo of him on someone's wall or in a restaurant. Obviously a black and white photo as it would have been taken in the 1950s. Or you might hear his name in the lyrics to a pop song, which would be something about looking like James Dean or smoking like James Dean, driving a fast car like James Dean, or just being cool like James Dean.
4.zh: 上世紀一些最著名藝術作品都有他。除了藝術，你可能在別人家中牆上或餐廳看過他的照片；當然是黑白照，因為拍於五十年代。又或者，你可能在流行曲歌詞中聽到他的名字，內容是像 James Dean 一樣的外貌、像他那樣抽煙、開快車，或者只是像他那麼酷。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: He is one of the most recognizable people of the last century. But why is he so recognizable? I mean, why is James Dean still so famous even today? Well, one of the things that ensured he would be a legend is that he died so young. He died at the age of 24, and so his good looks never faded. The other reason why his fame continues today is that he died tragically in a car crash.
4.zh: 他是上世紀最容易被認出的人之一。但為何如此？為什麼直到今天仍這麼有名？一個令他成為傳奇的原因，是他英年早逝：二十四歲就離世，因此俊朗外貌從未衰退。另一個讓他至今有名的原因，是他在車禍中悲劇性地喪生。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: This, I think, contributes significantly to his continuing fame. What's even more surprising is that James Dean wasn't one of those actors who made a lot of films. His fame rests on his roles in just three movies, and I'm going to talk about those in a moment. Actually, fame did not arrive so easily for James Dean. Before he made these three movies, he was involved in acting,
4.zh: 我認為這對他持續的名氣影響很大。更令人意外的是，他並不是拍了很多電影的演員。他的名氣建基於三部電影的角色，我稍後會談。其實他並非輕易成名；拍這三部電影之前，他已有演戲，

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: but only had small roles and he had to supplement his income with other jobs, such as a stunt tester on a TV game show called Beat the Clock. And he was actually fired. Why? It's quite ironic, really. In this TV show, contestants had to do stunts inside a certain time limit. One of the typical stunts was like, say, contestants had to pick up and carry an egg across a room in 30 seconds,
4.zh: 但只有小角色，要靠其他工作補貼收入，例如在電視遊戲節目 Beat the Clock 做特技測試員。他還被解僱了。為什麼？很諷刺。節目參賽者須在時限內完成特技，例如在三十秒內拿起一隻雞蛋並帶到房間另一邊，

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: but they weren't allowed to use their hands. That sort of thing. James Dean's job was as a stunt tester, so he had to test the stunts to see whether they would be possible to do inside the time limit. Actually, he was so good at doing the stunts and so quick that he was fired from the show.
4.zh: 但不准用手，就是這類項目。James Dean 的工作是測試特技是否能在時限內完成。可是他做得太好、太快，反而被節目解僱。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: As I said earlier, his fame rests on just three movies, East of Eden, Rebel Without a Cause, and Giant. It is the second of these movies, Rebel Without a Cause, filmed in 1955, that has been the most influential in popular culture. So what's so special about Rebel Without a Cause?
4.zh: 正如之前所說，他的名氣建基於三部電影：《天倫夢覺》、《阿飛正傳》和《巨人傳》。其中第二部、1955 年拍攝的《阿飛正傳》，對流行文化最有影響。它究竟有什麼特別？

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: Well, for the first time ever in the movies, Rebel Without a Cause showed the problems faced by a typical teenager in the 1950s. So what were these problems that teenagers faced back then? Well, they were pretty similar to those teenagers faced nowadays. But as I say, what made it special was that these problems had never been shown in movies before.
4.zh: 它是電影史上第一次呈現五十年代一般青少年面對的問題。當時青少年遇到什麼問題？其實與現今青少年很相似。但正如我所說，特別之處在於這些問題以前從未在電影中出現。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: Before that time, and I know this sounds crazy now, middle-aged adults usually had the leading roles. Young people played roles such as sons and daughters of the main characters. So why were young people even in movies? Well, young people were usually just there to show that the main characters, the adult characters, were happily married and had a happy family.
4.zh: 在此之前——我知道現在聽來很不可思議——主角通常是中年人，年輕人只扮演主角的兒女。那為何電影還要有年輕人？通常只是用來顯示成年主角婚姻美滿、家庭幸福。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: So typically, young people were on the screen for only five to ten minutes in the entire film. And that was it.
4.zh: 因此，年輕人在整部電影裡通常只出現五至十分鐘，僅此而已。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: James Dean and his role in Rebel Without a Cause changed all of that. It was as though Hollywood and the US movie-going public suddenly woke up. This had three huge effects on the movie industry. Firstly, a large number of movies about teenagers began to be made. Before this, as I said earlier, movies were always about adults.
4.zh: James Dean 在《阿飛正傳》中的角色改變了一切，彷彿荷里活與美國觀眾突然醒覺。這為電影業帶來三大影響。第一，開始大量製作關於青少年的電影；此前電影總是以成人為主題。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: The second major effect was that this kind of film began to be made in many different countries, so it wasn't just in Hollywood. It was in movie industries all over the world that films about teenagers started to be produced. And thirdly, and perhaps most importantly, young people, who had been ignored by the movie industry, were targeted as an audience by the movie industry. So young people became the target audience.
4.zh: 第二，許多不同國家開始製作這類電影，不再只是荷里活，而是世界各地電影業都開始拍青少年題材。第三，或許最重要的是，以前被忽略的年輕人，成為電影業針對的觀眾群，即目標觀眾。

4.speaker: David Stott
4.text: OK, let's fast forward 40 years to the rise of another movie star, Johnny Depp.
4.zh: 好的，現在快進四十年，談另一位影星 Johnny Depp 的崛起。

4.speaker: Exam Narrator
4.text: That is the end of task four. You now have two minutes to complete your answers to task four and to tidy up all your other answers.
4.zh: 任務四完結。你現在有兩分鐘完成任務四的答案，並整理其餘所有答案。

1.explanation: 第二款遊戲由 another one called 引出，名稱是 Ping Pong。它與 table tennis 類似，後者只是玩法說明，不是名稱。中伏位：Tennis for Two 已列為例子，不能再填；也不要把後面的新遊戲 Teen Queen Four 移到這一行。專有名稱建議按兩個單字書寫並用大寫。

2.explanation: Mrs Chau 在同一句把名稱及年份配對，說 Ping Pong from 1972，所以填 1972。from 在這裡標示遊戲的年代，而非國家來源。中伏位：1958 是已給例子的 Tennis for Two；2016 則屬較新的 Teen Queen Four。表格逐款遊戲記錄，必須把每個數字與正確名稱連在一起。

3.explanation: 家人轉問較新的遊戲時，爸爸直接報出 Teen Queen Four，Angela 亦重複確認。因此第三款遊戲填 Teen Queen Four，Four 可寫成 4。中伏位：爸爸稍後問有否 Teen Queen Five，但 Angela 否認現時有第五集；被問及的名稱不等於館內當年的遊戲。

4.explanation: Angela 說該遊戲是 this year, 2016 推出的，明確把第三款遊戲與 2016 年連結。題目 Year 只需填年份，不用再寫 this year。中伏位：next year 指爸爸詢問的 Teen Queen Five，不是第四集；不能按現實現在年份改答案，整段錄音的情境年份是 2016。

5.answer: it is closed on Wednesdays / it is closed today
5.explanation: 一家原本有興趣去電子遊戲博物館，爸爸查開放時間後才發現星期三休館，今天因此不能去。中伏位：這裡不去的原因不是博物館沉悶，因為 Angela 已改口認為它有趣；要聽最後決定的實際限制。可答 closed on Wednesdays，或結合當天情境寫 closed today。

6.explanation: 第二個建議明確叫 The Railway Museum，爸爸再重複一次。Railway 指鐵路，Museum 指博物館，合起來是機構名稱。中伏位：old station 是博物館所在建築，不是正式名稱；Museum of Youth Culture 是下一個方案。拼寫 railway，不要把 train ride 的活動代替名稱。

55.explanation: 講者說年輕角色通常只是用來顯示成年主角婚姻美滿、家庭幸福。因此答案要表達這個敘事功能。中伏位：不是展示年輕人的青春問題，那正是後來《阿飛正傳》的突破；也不是說年輕角色自己已婚。主語應是 adult main characters，避免把人物關係倒轉。
55.evidence: were happily married and had a happy family

56.answer: many more films about teenagers were made
56.explanation: 第一項影響是開始大量拍攝青少年題材電影，與此前總圍繞成人的電影對比。答案可寫 many more films about teenagers were made。中伏位：重點是電影題材轉向青年，不只是演員年齡下降；也不是只多拍 James Dean 本人的電影。第 56–58 題三項影響可交換次序。
56.evidence: a large number of movies about teenagers

57.answer: teenage films began to be made worldwide / in many countries
57.explanation: 第二項影響是青少年題材電影擴展到多個國家，不再只限荷里活。因此要寫在世界各地製作此類電影。中伏位：不是美國電影單純在海外放映，而是其他國家的電影業也開始製作；本格強調地理擴散，與前格數量增加不同，兩點不可合併後漏答。
57.evidence: this kind of film began to be made in many different countries

58.answer: young people became the target audience of the film industry
58.explanation: 第三項影響最關鍵：原本被電影業忽略的年輕人，成為目標觀眾。答案應寫 young people became the target audience。中伏位：target audience 指預期吸引來買票觀影的人，不是電影主角或演員；前兩格談製作的題材及地方，這格談市場對象，三者層次不同。
58.evidence: young people became the target audience
